description: Enforces `<repo-root>/.worktrees/` as the ONLY sanctioned worktree location (rig-cli AGENTS.md; GH-329: ~70 leftover worktrees scattered across five ad-hoc conventions, tens of GB of duplicated node_modules/.venv). BLOCKS a `git worktree add`/`move` whose target does not resolve under the repo's `.worktrees/` directory (`move` is gated on its destination — the second positional — so a legitimate migration INTO `.worktrees/` stays allowed), pointing the agent at `rig worktree create`/`rig worktree gc` instead. `git worktree remove` is NOT gated here: removal safety (landed + clean) is decided by the `block-unlanded-removal` hook. `rig worktree create`'s own internal `git worktree add` call is a plain subprocess spawned from inside the `rig` process, never routed through the agent's own Bash tool, so this hook never sees it and needs no process-ancestry trust mechanism (verified against riglib/worktree.py). `git worktree prune`/`list`/`lock`/`unlock`/`repair` are out of scope (see module docstring). Repo root resolved via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, honoring a `-C`/`--git-dir`/`GIT_DIR=` override on the gated command so a cross-repo or explicit-git-dir invocation is judged against the real target repo, not a fail-open 'undetermined'. No opt-in flag: installed everywhere the catalog is applied, like block-raw-pr-merge/block-no-verify. Deny-by-default; no self-service env-var bypass. RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_BLOCK_RAW_WORKTREE_ADD requests one Telegram approval (deny-by-default; a bare `1` is rejected), same pattern as block-raw-pr-merge — capped at ONE hatch round-trip per invocation, so a chained command with more than one gate-worthy segment blocks the later ones outright rather than risk a multi-call timeout overrun silently allowing the whole chain. timeout_ms 960000 covers the hatch helper's 930s worst case (tg-ctl ask's 900s cap plus a 30s margin); a Claude Code settings entry launching cc_hook_bridge must also set timeout >960s. on_error=open: a git/parse failure fails open — this is workflow discipline (where a worktree lands), not a security boundary, matching the sibling pin-primary-worktree/worktree-only-writes hooks rather than block-raw-pr-merge's on_error=closed.
